Brand overview & key differentiators vs traditional energy
Asked for an overview of the Celsius brand and the key differentiators of its brand equity versus traditional energy.

Framed Celsius around three megatrends - better-for-you (7 vitamins, no aspartame/HFCS), function (six clinical studies, thermogenic), and fitness (brand DNA). Likened to Athleisure evolution; positioned as Energy 2.0. Differentiated by usage occasion (pairs with meals, acts as a functional soda); foodservice ~11% of Pepsi sales, national Jersey Mike's rollout. Biggest known opportunity entering Pepsi was closing the ~60% convenience/gas ACV gap.
Whether there is scope for a lower-caffeine version and whether the brand has 'broader shoulders' than traditional energy.

Yes - a cross-functional team manages a three-to-five-year portfolio strategy; timing and sequencing key. Aims to build Celsius into a global iconic brand able to enter adjacencies (functional seltzers, hydration, health/wellness), but current focus stays on energy.
Whether there is a different value proposition in the lifetime value of a Celsius consumer versus the legacy category.

Celsius grew up in fitness, repositioned in 2017 as a better-for-you essential energy product. The 'live fit' mantra and multiple usage occasions (pre-workout, lunch, afternoon) drive higher consumer value; numerator data shows substantial new-to-category share.
What drives incremental category spend and where Celsius sources its volume (the 'other 60%').

Volume from CSDs and curious consumers seeking energy/functionality; category growing 10-15%. ~60/40 male/female mix in convenience (vs ~70/30 norm). Numerator: 44% new-to-category (younger from CSDs, older from coffee/tea) and ~40% user intensification. Incrementality, not brand-shifting, is what matters; South Florida share to 23.5% from 21.7% a brick-and-mortar proof point.
Channels best positioned for incremental sales
Whether certain channels are better situated to drive incremental sales versus others.

At 95% ACV, significant runway in activating existing stores - second/third placements, better cooler placement. Strong Q2 club and Amazon growth; independents a big opportunity. Cooler/secondary placement initiatives and foodservice still early-stage; entering buyer meetings at ~10 share vs 3.4 last year improves prioritization.
How management feels about inventory levels in the system and ability to keep up with latent demand.

Works with the largest global suppliers/can manufacturers with secondary routes; 17+ co-packers (~22 with flex capacity); confident on supply. Real challenge is managing growth (SKUs up 200-300%) and out-of-orbit shipping raising COGS/freight, with optimization plans in place. Ops head Paul Storey ex-Monster/Rockstar.
Reflections on the initial PepsiCo transition.

Transition went far better than anticipated; advantage that many Celsius team members previously worked at Pepsi; ~80% of distribution transferred at one point in time (vs others' messier staggered cutoffs). Fieldly was the only allied-brand person allowed to speak on stage at Pepsi's national meeting in Dallas.
Drivers of ACV growth and of club/e-commerce growth; with ACV at 95%, what are the key focus areas for 2024.

Surprising that club and online kept growing as ACV/SKUs expanded - 'all tides are rising' with no cannibalization, aided by user intensification and a shift toward cold availability. ~$250M club/Costco/Amazon run rate; Amazon up over 100% last quarter (#2); #1 on Instacart. 2024: first-time inclusion in PepsiCo national AOP, more marketing dollars than ever, MLS deal (Inter Miami, Messi), PFL partnership, Live Fit Tour.
Given South Florida share growth in mature markets, how the approach varies between mature and up-and-coming markets.

Growth rates similar - difference is the starting basis. Drill-deep legacy markets over-index; non-legacy markets start lower and grow faster initially before settling into similar rates. Brand awareness expansion is the answer to 'what's next' beyond 95% ACV - Celsius is nowhere near Monster/Red Bull awareness.
Continuation - how approach varies and what comes next at 95% ACV.

In 2024, Celsius will expand its number of focus markets; with PepsiCo it can set up distribution, placements, displays, and marketing overlay to activate markets faster and see share gains and investment returns.

Given Q2 EBITDA margin just under 24% and a 1,000 bps gross margin increase, how to think about the longer-term operating margin run rate as growth normalizes - does it migrate toward a large incumbent peer.

Margins can get very close if not similar to a public peer, but the peer classifies outbound freight in sales expense vs Celsius's COGS - requires adjustment. Q2 S&M ~19% vs preferred 21-22%; disciplined ROI-driven playbook. 2024 S&M could move toward ~20-22% to leverage new distribution; now is not the time to pull back.
How investors should think about Celsius's appetite for international expansion, the timeline, and priorities for new market entry.

Massive US runway plus international opportunity - 10+ share in Sweden, growing Finland, recent launches in South Korea/Taiwan; larger markets (UK, Canada, Australia, Japan) under evaluation. Finalizing two countries - Canada priority #1 for 2024, another announced soon. Methodical, fitness/health-focused; David framed it as a three-to-five-year-plus effort with a larger rollout in 2025; US remains the priority.
